issue_context.title: Replace strings with resources in Mono corelib
issue_context.body:
In src\mono\netcore\System.Private.CoreLib the pattern `Exception\s\("` has 340 hits. All these strings should instead come from src\libraries\System.Private.CoreLib\src\Resources\Strings.resx somewhere. In most cases there are already equivalent strings that can be determined by brief inspection of equivalent code in src\coreclr\src\System.Private.CoreLib or possibly src\libraries\System.Private.CoreLib. 

Sometimes the strings need adjustment eg `throw new ArgumentException ("type is not TypeBuilder but " + type.GetType (), "type");` vs `throw new ArgumentException(SR.Argument_MustBeTypeBuilder);`. 

Some strings are in native code in coreclr eg `throw new SynchronizationLockException ("Object is not synchronized");` is not thrown in Monitor.cs in coreclr. In this case it can just be `throw new SynchronizationLockException()`

A (very?) few may need new strings.

There are also a few trivial cases where the string should be replaced with `nameof` eg `throw new ArgumentException("className")` -> `throw new ArgumentException(nameof(className))`
comments: Also some are grandfathered in, as in coreclr. Eg., `throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException("requiredLength", SR.ArgumentOutOfRange_SmallCapacity);` in StringBuilder is "requiredLength" forever presumably.

With a slightly relaxed pattern, it also captures the cases where the first argument is `nameof()` followed by a hard-coded string:

```sh
$ git grep "Exception.*\""  :/src/mono/netcore/System.Private.CoreLib/src/*.cs | wc -l

443
```

> StringBuilder is "requiredLength" forever presumably

Is there a reason for it? We have fixed many similar bugs over the years, I do not see a reason why not to fix this one.
If you do not recall this kind of change breaking things, lets do it.

I am not sure this is a step in right direction. We'll probably have to do work in the opposite direction and remove all resources overhead to cut on the size on workloads where English support is enough.

Every other assembly as well as the coreclr corelib build uses resources, as does 95% of the mono corelib via shared sources. Plus we want error messages to be the same across builds and not have to update them in many places when they change. I agree it'd be valid for the linker to optionally inline resource strings (or some other build step doing it), but that would be in addition to rather than instead of consistency in this last mile.

>Every other assembly as well as the coreclr corelib build uses resources, as does 95% of the mono corelib via shared sources.

I am aware of that and that would be unfortunate size regression if we had to ship with that (made tracking issue for that as #34057 a bit earlier).

@marek-safar thanks for pointing this out. Would you have any reason for concern if your https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/34057 is completed? It seems like these strings would be a small issue in comparison so that work likely is inevitable.

> I am aware of that and that would be unfortunate size regression if we had to ship with that (made tracking issue for that as #34057 a bit earlier).

Understood, and not disagreeing.  That's why I said such work "would be in addition to rather than instead of" this.
@danmosemsft I am not against someone doing the work
@eerhardt @vitek-karas is it safe to assume that the linker work will include #34057  ?

> I am not sure this is a step in right direction. We'll probably have to do work in the opposite direction and remove all resources overhead to cut on the size on workloads where English support is enough.

Just for the record, UI validation and databinding usually requires localized exception texts, at least on WinForms and WPF frameworks, but probably other frameworks as well. No idea if thats relevant in Mono, just thought I'd mention it to make people aware if they aren't.

> In src\mono\netcore\System.Private.CoreLib the pattern Exception\s\(" has 340 hits. 

fwiw `Exception\s*\(` in src\mono\System.Private.CoreLib is down to 205 hits as of now.

@danmoseley @marek-safar, I see that there are some exception that contain certain keywords related to time units (e.g. ticks, milliseconds, etc.) in System.DateTime. Should these be added to the resource dictionary too?

@tudoranghelina91 the strings (the exception messages) should be in the resources, yes. Those messages would include words like "ticks" and localizers can decide how to translate them.

If you mean the "parameter name" parameter to ArgumentExceptions-- those are not localized and do not go in resources. They should match the API.

Hey @danmoseley Sorry to bother you again. I am a bit confused regarding ArgumentExceptions. Which prefix to use? Argument or ArgumentException? is Argument prefix the same as ArgumentException prefix?
Hello, I'm not sure what you're referring to. Could you give me some links into the places in the code?

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e09903f9b1bee58e5def96007e9fd743685ef8e2/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/Resources/Strings.resx#L190

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e09903f9b1bee58e5def96007e9fd743685ef8e2/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/Resources/Strings.resx#L1531

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e09903f9b1bee58e5def96007e9fd743685ef8e2/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/Resources/Strings.resx#L1528

What's the difference between the prefixes of these 3 lines? I am talking about the name attribute
Yes, we are not consistent in using prefixes for resource strings. Pick the one that makes the most sense to you.
